_comment: Canonical fast-moving facts the mcp-ops skill encodes. scripts/check-mcp-facts.py asserts the skill prose still names these SDK packages + spec URL and still carries a dated currency note (--offline), and probes the npm/PyPI registries + the spec URL for drift (--live). Edit deliberately: a change here is a skill-content decision, not housekeeping. 2026-10-22 refresh: spec 2026-07-28, Python SDK v2, FastMCP 4 and the TS SDK v2 package split - sources in references/v2-migration.md.

spec._comment: The MCP specification URL cited in See Also (moved off the spec. subdomain, which stopped resolving by 2026-07). --offline asserts the token is named in the skill prose; --live expects the URL to answer HTTP 200 (after redirects). 'revision' is informational: the newest spec revision the skill teaches (sessionless requests, server/discover, no server-to-client requests).

@modelcontextprotocol/server.role: TypeScript SDK v2, server side (split out of the v1 @modelcontextprotocol/sdk monolith)
@modelcontextprotocol/server._comment: What the TypeScript samples import (McpServer, registerTool, createMcpHandler, serveStdio from ./stdio). 2.3.1 on 2026-10-05; first 2.0.0 2026-07-27. A 3.x would be an API-break release warranting a skill review.

@modelcontextprotocol/client._comment: Used by the testing reference (Client, StreamableHTTPClientTransport). Versions in lock-step with @modelcontextprotocol/server.

@modelcontextprotocol/sdk.role: TypeScript SDK v1 monolith - still published on the 1.x line (1.32.1 on 2026-10-05); v2 lives in the split packages above
@modelcontextprotocol/sdk._comment: Named in the skill as the v1 package to migrate from. Tracked at major 1: if it ever publishes a 2.x the split-package story in the skill needs a re-check.

@modelcontextprotocol/codemod._comment: Resolution-only check: a 404 means the migration command the skill teaches is gone.

@modelcontextprotocol/inspector._comment: The interactive inspector invoked via `npx`; v2 line (2.12.0 on 2026-10-22, Node >=22.19). Only resolution is checked live; a 404 means it was renamed/removed.

mcp.role: Python SDK (high-level MCPServer, formerly FastMCP; mcp.server.fastmcp removed in 2.0)
mcp._comment: The official Python SDK on PyPI, installed via `uv add "mcp[cli]"`. 2.3.0 on 2026-10-02; 1.x is maintenance-only on the v1.x branch. --live flags drift if the latest release leaves major 2.

fastmcp._comment: The standalone FastMCP package, documented at major 4 (built on SDK v2; server-pushed sampling/roots removed, ctx.elicit legacy-only, tasks as an extension). 4.1.3 on 2026-10-20. Named in prose as FastMCP and via gofastmcp.com; matched case-insensitively.
